insights.claim: All 35 admission webhooks use failurePolicy: Fail, creating a hard availability dependency between the kueue-controller-manager and workload submission across the cluster.
insights.reasoning: With failurePolicy: Fail on all webhook configurations, any unavailability of the kueue-controller-manager (pod crash, node drain, certificate expiry) will block creation and update of Jobs, Deployments, StatefulSets, Pods, and all ML training workloads cluster-wide. The single-replica deployment (replicas: 1) provides no redundancy.

insights.claim: The kueue-operator build uses -tags strictfipsruntime, enforcing FIPS-compliant cryptography at the Go runtime level when running on a FIPS-enabled host.
insights.reasoning: The strictfipsruntime build tag causes the Go runtime to panic if FIPS mode is required by the host but the binary cannot satisfy it, providing a fail-closed FIPS guarantee rather than silent degradation.

insights.claim: Kueue's RBAC and webhook scope covers 8 distinct workload API groups (batch, kubeflow.org, ray.io, jobset.x-k8s.io, leaderworkerset.x-k8s.io, workload.codeflare.dev, apps, core), making it a cross-cutting dependency for most ML and batch workload types in the platform.
insights.reasoning: The kueue-manager-role ClusterRole and the webhook configurations grant access to resources from 8 different API groups. Any component deploying workloads of these types will have its creation flow intercepted by Kueue webhooks for admission control.
